fullData.title: Adding Decimals on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Leo walks $0.4$ miles to the park, and then walks another $0.3$ miles to the library. Use the number line to show his total distance walked, and find the sum $0.4 + 0.3$.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Count forward along the number line in tenths to find the total distance.

content.imagePrompt: A clean educational number line from 0 to 1 divided into ten equal parts marked in tenths. An arrow starts at 0 and jumps 4 steps to 0.4 labeled Park. Another arrow starts at 0.4 and jumps 3 more steps to 0.7 labeled Library. Bright primary colors against a white background.
content.altText: A number line showing two jumps, first from 0 to 0.4 and then 3 more tenths to 0.7.

labels.description: Jump four tenths from zero to reach zero point four.
Jump three more tenths to land on zero point seven.

annotations.steps: Start at zero, jump right four tenths to zero point four, then jump three more tenths to zero point seven.
annotations.strategy: I notice that using a number line helps me add decimals by counting jumps just like whole numbers.
annotations.misconceptions: Students often count the tick marks instead of the spaces or jumps between them, leading to an off-by-one error.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition directly to whole number addition on a number line, showing that tenths work just like ones.
annotations.narrative: On Figure 1, start at $\text{Start}$ at $0$ and move right $4$ tenths to the point labeled $\text{Park}$ at $0.4$. From $0.4$, count $3$ more tenths to the right to reach the point labeled $\text{Library}$ at $0.7$.

challenge.prompt: Leo starts at 0 and jumps 4 tenths to 0.4. If he jumps 3 more tenths forward along the number line, on what number will he land?
challenge.rationale: Counting 3 spaces forward from 0.4 lands on 0.7; counting tick marks instead of the spaces between them leads to an off-by-one error like 0.6 or 0.8.

challenge.prompt: Now write the total distance as an addition sentence: what is the sum when you add 0.4 and 0.3?
challenge.rationale: Adding 4 tenths and 3 tenths yields 7 tenths ($0.7$); adding the digits as whole numbers without decimal place value incorrectly gives $7$ or $70$.

annotations.steps: Add four tenths and three tenths to get seven tenths.
annotations.strategy: I notice we can just add the tenth parts together like whole numbers.
annotations.misconceptions: A common mistake is adding the numbers as whole numbers to get four plus three equals seven, but forgetting the decimal point makes it seventy instead of zero point seven.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition directly to counting fractional parts on a number line.
annotations.narrative: Adding $4$ tenths and $3$ tenths gives $7$ tenths. Therefore, the sum is $0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7$, meaning Leo walked a total of $0.7$ miles.

specs.title: Trace distances on number line
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Visualize decimal addition as sequential forward jumps marked in tenths along a number line.
specs.seedNotes: Show a number line marked in tenths from 0 to 1 with an initial jump of 0.4 from 0 to 'Park' and a second jump of 0.3 ending at 'Library' at 0.7.

specs.title: Calculate the total distance
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Connect visual number line hops to place-value decimal addition of tenths.
specs.seedNotes: Express the sum of 4 tenths and 3 tenths as 7 tenths, resulting in the equation $0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7$ miles.
